alignments.note: The copula is expressed; interrogative inversion is English word order and does not move it (rule 53's refusal).

Corrected from *the*. Rule 20 with rule 57's closing clause: the English *carpenter's* already occupies the determiner slot of the head noun *son*, exactly as tes Kaisaros oikias -> *Caesar's household* leaves its article empty, so the article governing huios realizes nothing. The single English *the* stands in front of *carpenter*, not in front of *son*, and belongs to that noun's own article s005.

Corrected from unrepresented. Rules 19 and 57: the interposed genitive keeps its own article, and the determiner the ASV writes before *carpenter* is what that article realizes. 13:15 is the control in the same chapter: there the inner article is emptied only because *this* fills the slot before *people*, which is rule 38 doing what a written *the* would otherwise leave to the article.
Genitive noun rendered with *'s*, which is what displaces s004 under rule 20.
The head noun stands bare, its determiner slot taken by the possessive.
The genitive pronoun takes the possessive that empties s009.
Discontinuous *is ... called* under rule 15, headed on the lexical verb under rule 17.
Names are split separately under rule 17.

review_notes: The two articles of ho tou tektonos huios were swapped: the accepted alignment gave *the* to the head noun's article and emptied the genitive's article. Rule 20 empties an article whose noun's determiner slot is taken by an English *'s*, and the *the* the ASV wrote determines *carpenter*, which is the genitive's own noun.

Reading *the* as the determiner of the whole phrase *the carpenter's son*, and so as the outer article's, is the competing analysis; it is refused because rule 20 names the *'s* displacement in terms and rule 57 cites tes Kaisaros oikias for exactly this shape.
13:15's this people's heart is the chapter's control and is analysed the same way: the inner article is decided by the determiner standing in front of the inner noun.
Everything else in the verse is unchanged, including ouchi taking *not* under rule 64 and the discontinuous *is ... called* on s012.
